```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
```

## 1. Model Definition

This model simulates a population with age structure under food production constraints.

```{r}
food_limited <- odin.dust::odin_dust({
  # Include external C++ function
  config(include) <- "pgamma.cpp"
  
  dt <- user(1)
  
  # Model dimensions
  n_age <- user(120)
  
  # Initial conditions
  initial(pop[]) <- pop_init[i]
  
  # Production parameters
  yield_base <- user(13100 * 365)      # Base yield (kcal/ha/year)
  land_max <- user(1000)         # Maximum arable land
  work_hours <- user(5)          # Hours devoted to agriculture per day
  land_per_hour <- user(0.0944)  # Area cultivated per worker-hour (ha/worker-hour)
  cal_max <- user(2785 * 365)          # Maximum yearly caloric requirement
  set_aside <- user(0)         # Yield proportion set aside 
  alpha <- user(0.12)  # annual decay rate of food in storage
  
  # Age-specific parameters
  work_capacity[] <- user()      # Age-specific work capacity (0-1)
  food_need[] <- user()          # Age-specific relative food needs
  surv_base[] <- user()          # Base survival rates
  fert_base[] <- user()          # Base fertility rates
  pop_init[] <- user()           # Initial population distribution
  surv_shape[] <- user()         # Survival shape parameters
  
  # Set dimensions for age-specific vectors
  dim(work_capacity) <- n_age
  dim(food_need) <- n_age
  dim(surv_base) <- n_age
  dim(fert_base) <- n_age
  dim(pop_init) <- n_age
  dim(surv_shape) <- n_age
  
  # Calculate workforce and consumption
  workers[] <- pop[i] * work_capacity[i]
  dim(workers) <- n_age
  total_workers <- sum(workers)
  
  cal_need[] <- pop[i] * cal_max * food_need[i]
  dim(cal_need) <- n_age
  total_cal_need <- sum(cal_need) * dt # scale to time step
  
  # Yield variation as fraction of base yield
  yield_var[] <- user() 
  dim(yield_var) <- user()
  yield_actual <- yield_base * if (as.integer(step) >= length(yield_var)) yield_var[length(yield_var)] else yield_var[step + 1]
  
  # Food production with stochastic variation and land limitation
  land_used <- 1 - exp(-land_per_hour * work_hours * total_workers / land_max)
  #yield_actual <- rgamma(1 / (yield_var^2), yield_base * (yield_var^2))
  food_prod <- yield_actual * land_max * land_used * (1 - set_aside) * dt # scale to time step
  
  # Food availability ratio
  food_ratio <- (food_prod) / total_cal_need
  #surplus <- food_prod - total_cal_need
  
  # Vital rates responsive to food ratio
  fert_actual[] <- fert_base[i] * pgamma_cpp(food_ratio, 4.579627264, 0.1)
  mort_rate[] <- 1 - (surv_base[i] * pgamma_cpp(food_ratio, surv_shape[i], 0.1))
  
  # Population dynamics
  births_by_age[] <- rbinom(pop[i], 1 - (1 - fert_actual[i])^dt)
  total_births <- sum(births_by_age)
  deaths[] <- rbinom(pop[i], 1 - (1 - mort_rate[i])^dt) # sub-step scaling of probabilities
  pop_surviving[] <- pop[i] - deaths[i]
  
  # Aging
  aging_up[] <- rbinom(pop_surviving[i], dt)
  dim(aging_up) <- n_age
  
  # Set dimensions for dynamic variables
  dim(births_by_age) <- n_age
  dim(mort_rate) <- n_age
  dim(fert_actual) <- n_age
  dim(deaths) <- n_age
  dim(pop_surviving) <- n_age
  dim(pop) <- n_age
  
  # Update equations -- double check this is correct!
  update(pop[1]) <- pop_surviving[1] - aging_up[1] + total_births
  update(pop[2:(n_age-1)]) <- (pop_surviving[i] - aging_up[i]) + aging_up[i-1]
  update(pop[n_age]) <- pop_surviving[n_age] + aging_up[n_age - 1]
  
  update(food_stored) <- food_stored + food_prod - total_cal_need - alpha * food_stored * dt
  update(food_ratio_out) <- food_ratio
  #update(surplus_out) <- surplus
  update(delta_N) <- total_births - sum(deaths)
  initial(food_stored) <- 0
 # initial(surplus_out) <- 0
  initial(delta_N) <- 0
  initial(food_ratio_out) <- 1
  
}, verbose = FALSE)
```

## 2. Yield Forcing Functions

Functions to generate and interpolate yield variation over time.

```{r yield_forcing}
# Generate n years of yield multipliers
generate_yield_forcing <- function(n_years, yield_var = 0.3, seed = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)
  
  rgamma(n_years,
         shape = 1 / (yield_var^2),
         scale = 1 * (yield_var^2))  # Using 1 as base to get multipliers
}

# Interpolate annual yield values to finer time steps
interpolate_yield_forcing <- function(annual_forcing, time_step = "monthly") {
  n_years <- length(annual_forcing)
  
  # Create time vectors
  annual_times <- 1:n_years
  
  periods_per_year <- switch(time_step,
                           "monthly" = 12,
                           "weekly" = 52,
                           "daily" = 365)
  
  fine_times <- seq(1, n_years, length.out = n_years * periods_per_year)
  
  # Interpolation using splines
  spline(annual_times, annual_forcing, n = length(fine_times))$y
}
```

## 3. Simulation Setup

Configure and run the simulation.

```{r simulation_setup}
# Simulation parameters
n_particles <- 50
dt <- 1
years <- 600
timesteps <- 1:(dt ^ -1 * years)

# Generate yield forcing
annual_forcing <- generate_yield_forcing(years, seed = 123)

# Load demographic parameters
pars <- read_csv('../../Models/spacelim-master/demog_vectors.csv') %>%
  mutate(age = 0:119)

n_age <- 120

# Define work capacity by age (manually defined vector)
work_capacity_vector <- c(
  rep(0, 6),                                # Ages 0-5: No work
  seq(0.1, 0.15, length.out = 4),           # Ages 6-9: Limited work
  seq(0.2, 0.3, length.out = 3),            # Ages 10-12: More capacity
  seq(0.4, 0.5, length.out = 2),            # Ages 13-14: Adolescent work
  rep(1, 41),                               # Ages 15-55: Full capacity
  seq(0.8, 0.6, length.out = 10),           # Ages 56-65: Declining capacity
  seq(0.4, 0.3, length.out = 5),            # Ages 66-70: Elderly work
  seq(0.2, 0, length.out = 15),             # Ages 71-85: Minimal to no work
  rep(0, 34)                                # Ages 86+: No work
)

# Parameter list for model
par_list <- list(
  pop_init = c(rep(0, 20), 20, rep(0, 99)),  # Start with 20 people at age 20
  fert_base = pars$mstar,                    # Base fertility rates
  surv_shape = pars$mortparms,               # Survival shape parameters
  surv_base = pars$pstar,                    # Base survival rates
  work_capacity = work_capacity_vector,      # Age-specific work capacity
  food_need = pars$rho,                      # Age-specific food needs
  area_max = 2500, #6500,                           # Maximum area (65km² with 5km hex sides)
  n_age = 120,
  yield_base = 7000000,#7000 * 365,                   # Base yield (kcal/ha/year)
  work_hours = 1, #8,                            # Daily work hours
  land_per_hour = 1, #2.3,                       # Area cultivated per worker-hour
  yield_var = annual_forcing,                # Annual yield variation
  dt = dt,                                   # Time step
  set_aside = 0                              # No food set aside
)

# Initialize and run model
mod <- food_limited$new(
  pars = par_list,
  time = 1L,
  n_particles = n_particles,
  seed = 6L
)

# Run simulation
state <- mod$simulate(timesteps) %>%
  array(
    dim = c(n_age + 3, n_particles, length(timesteps)),
    dimnames = list(
      age = c('food_stored', 'delta_N', 'e', 0:(n_age - 1)),
      rep = 1:n_particles,
      time = timesteps * dt
    )
  ) %>%
  cubelyr::as.tbl_cube(met_name = 'value') %>%
  as_tibble()
```

## 4. Visualizations

### 4.1 Total Population Over Time

```{r population_over_time}
state %>%
  filter(!(age %in% c('food_stored', 'e', 'surplus', 'delta_N'))) %>%
  group_by(rep, time) %>%
  summarize(N = sum(value)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(time, N / par_list$area_max , group = rep)) +  #/ 6500
  geom_line(alpha = 0.1) +
  labs(
    title = "Population Density Over Time",
    x = "Time (years)",
    y = "Population density (persons/ha)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
ggsave('pop_trajectory.png', width = 6, height = 4, bg = 'white')
```

### 4.2 Population by Age Group

```{r population_by_age_group}
state %>%
  filter(!(age %in% c('food_stored', 'e', 'surplus', 'delta_N'))) %>%
  mutate(age_group = cut(
    as.numeric(age),
    breaks = c(0, 4, 14, 64, Inf),
    labels = c("0-4", "5-14", "15-64", "65+"),
    right = FALSE  # Makes intervals [0,5), [5,15), etc.
  )) %>%
  group_by(rep, time, age_group) %>%
  summarize(N = sum(value), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  ggplot(aes(time, N / par_list$area_max, group = interaction(rep, age_group), color = age_group)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.1) +
  labs(
    title = "Population by Age Group",
    x = "Time (years)",
    y = "Population density (persons/ha)",
    color = "Age Group"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
ggsave('pop_trajectory_ages.png', width = 6, height = 4, bg = 'white')
```

### 4.3 Food Storage


```{r age_structure}
state %>%
  filter(!(age %in% c('food_stored', 'e', 'surplus', 'delta_N'))) %>%
  filter(time %in% seq(1, 600, 50)) %>%
  mutate(age = as.numeric(age)) %>%
  filter(age <= 99) %>%
  filter(rep == 1) %>%
  # Create 5-year age groups
  mutate(age_group = 5 * floor(age/5)) %>%
  # Sum values within each age group
  group_by(time, age_group) %>%
  summarize(value = sum(value), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  ggplot(aes(age_group, value)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~time, scales = 'free_y') +
  labs(
    title = "Age Structure at Over Time",
    x = "Age Group (5-year intervals)",
    y = "Population"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

### 4.5 Dependency Ratio

```{r dependency_ratio}
state %>%
  filter(!(age %in% c('food_stored', 'e', 'surplus', 'delta_N'))) %>%
  mutate(workers = between(as.numeric(age), 15, 65)) %>%
  group_by(rep, time, workers) %>%
  summarize(value = sum(value), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = workers) %>%
  mutate(dependency_ratio = `FALSE` / `TRUE`) %>%
  ggplot(aes(time, dependency_ratio, group = rep)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.1) +
  labs(
```

### Juvenility Index

```{r}
state %>%
  filter(!(age %in% c('food_stored', 'e', 'surplus', 'delta_N'))) %>%
  mutate(age_group = cut(
    as.numeric(age),
    breaks = c(0, 4, 14, 19, Inf),
    labels = c("infants", "juveniles", "teens", "adults"),
    right = FALSE  # Makes intervals [0,5), [5,15), etc.
  )) %>%
  group_by(rep, time, age_group) %>%
  summarize(N = sum(value), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = age_group, values_from = N) |>
  mutate(ji = juveniles / adults) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, ji, group = rep)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.1) +
  labs(
    title = "Juvenility Index Over Time",
    x = "Time (years)",
    y = "Juvenility Index (juveniles / adults)"
```

### 4.8 Transition Times

```{r transition_times}
# First transition to food ratio < 1
state %>%
  filter(age == 'e') %>%
  filter(value < 1) %>%
  group_by(rep) %>%
  filter(time == min(time)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(time)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "First Transition to Food Ratio < 1",
    x = "Time (years)",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

# First transition to food ratio ≤ 0.67 (more severe shortage)
state %>%
  filter(age == 'e') %>%
  filter(value <= 0.67) %>%
  group_by(rep) %>%
  filter(time == min(time)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(time)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "darkred") +
  labs(
    title = "First Transition to Food Ratio ≤ 0.67",
    x = "Time (years)",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

### 4.10 Combined Key Metrics

```{r combined_metrics, fig.width = 7, fig.asp = 1}
# Create food ratio plot
food_ratio_plot <- state %>%
  filter(age == 'e') %>%
  ggplot(aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.1, aes(group = rep)) +
  geom_smooth(color = "blue") +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 1), color = 'red', linetype = 2) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Food Availability",
    y = 'Food Ratio'
  )

# Create population plot
pop_plot <- state %>%
  filter(!(age %in% c('food_stored', 'e', 'surplus', 'delta_N'))) %>%
  group_by(rep, time) %>%
  summarize(N = sum(value), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  ggplot(aes(time, N)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.1, aes(group = rep)) +
  geom_smooth(color = "green") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Total Population",
    y = 'Persons'
  )

# Create growth rate plot
growth_plot <- state %>%
  filter(!(age %in% c('e', 'surplus', 'delta_N', 'food_stored'))) %>%
  group_by(rep, time) %>%
  summarize(N = sum(value)) %>%
  mutate(growth_rate = (N - lag(N))) %>%
  ungroup() |>
  ggplot(aes(time, growth_rate)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.1, aes(group = rep)) +
  geom_smooth(color = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Population Growth",
    y = 'Persons/year'
  )

storage_plot <- state %>%
  filter(age == 'food_stored') %>%
  ggplot(aes(time, value / (2785 * 365))) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.1, aes( group = rep)) +
  labs(
    title = "Food Surplus",
    x = "Time (years)",
    y = "Rations"
  ) +
   geom_line(alpha = 0.1, aes(group = rep)) +
  geom_smooth(color = "purple") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = 'red') +
  theme_bw()

# Combine plots
library(patchwork)
pop_plot / food_ratio_plot / growth_plot / storage_plot +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1, 1, 1)) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Key Population Dynamics Metrics",
    caption = "Smoothed trends across all simulation runs"
  )
```

## 5. Elasticity Analysis

```{r elasticity}
# Survival elasticity by age and food ratio
expand_grid(age = 0:100, e = seq(0, 1.2, 0.01)) %>%
  left_join(pars) %>%
  mutate(elasticity = pgamma(e, mortparms, scale = 0.1),
         survival = pstar * elasticity) %>%
  ggplot(aes(e, survival, group = age, color = age)) +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Survival Rate by Age and Food Ratio",
    x = "Food Ratio",
    y = "Survival Rate",
    color = "Age"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

# Mortality elasticity
expand_grid(age = 0:100, e = seq(0, 1.2, 0.01)) %>%
  left_join(pars) %>%
  mutate(elasticity = pgamma(e, mortparms, scale = 0.1),
         survival = pstar * elasticity) %>%
  ggplot(aes(e, 1 - survival, group = age, color = age)) +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Mortality Rate by Age and Food Ratio",
    x = "Food Ratio",
    y = "Mortality Rate",
    color = "Age"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
ggsave('mortality_elasticity.png', width = 6, height = 4, bg = 'white')
```

## 6. Notes and Future Improvements

The model currently doesn't incorporate several potentially important factors: - Food storage dynamics (currently implemented simplistically) - Spoilage mechanisms beyond basic decay rate - Seed reserves for future planting - Taxation or tithing effects - Seasonal or periodic work patterns - Sex/gender divisions in labor - Land fallowing practices

Target population range for this area based on historical estimates: 5,200 - 19,500 people.
